question: The definitions in an XML document are said to be __________ when the tagging system and definitions in the DTD are all in compliance.
explanation: A document that conforms to its DTD is valid; well-formed only means it obeys XML syntax.

options.B: M=3; D1 displays "6"; D2 displays "12"; D3 displays "6".

question:
In Java, which of the following statements is/are True ?
S1 : The ‘final’ keyword applied to a class definition prevents the class from being extended through derivation.
S2 : A class can only inherit one class but can implement multiple interfaces.
S3 : Java permits a class to replace the implementation of a method that it has inherited. It is called method overloading.

options.D: All of S1, S2 and S3

explanation: S3 describes overriding, not overloading.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are True ?
P: C programming language has a weak type system with static types.
Q: Java programming language has a strong type system with static types.
explanation: C is statically but weakly typed (implicit conversions, casts); Java is statically and strongly typed.

question: A graphic display system has a frame buffer that is 640 pixels wide, 480 pixels high and 1 bit of color depth. If the access time for each pixel on the average is 200 nanoseconds, then the refresh rate of this frame buffer is approximately :
explanation: 640 × 480 × 200 ns = 0.06144 s per frame, about 16.3 frames per second.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are True regarding the solution to the visibility problem in 3D graphics ?
S1 : The Painter's algorithm sorts polygons by depth and then paints (scan - converts) each Polygon on to the screen starting with the most nearest polygon.
S2 : Backface Culling refers to eliminating geometry with backfacing normals.
explanation: The painter's algorithm paints from the farthest polygon to the nearest, so S1 is false; S2 is correct.

question: Consider the matrix M = [[2, 0, 2], [0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 1]] representing a set of planar (2D) geometric transformations in homogeneous coordinates. Which of the following statements about the matrix M is True ?

options.A: M represents first, a scaling of vector (2, 1) followed by translation of vector (1, 1)
options.B: M represents first, a translation of vector (1, 1) followed by scaling of vector (2, 1)
options.C: M represents first, a scaling of vector (3, 1) followed by shearing of parameters (−1, 1)
options.D: M represents first, a shearing of parameters (−1, 1) followed by scaling of vector (3, 1)

explanation: S(2,1)·T(1,1) = [[2,0,2],[0,1,1],[0,0,1]], i.e. translate first, then scale. Scale-then-translate would give [[2,0,1],[0,1,1]].

question:
Assume the following regarding the development of a software system P :
- Estimated lines of code of P : 33, 480 LOC
- Average productivity for P : 620 LOC per person-month
- Number of software developers : 6
- Average salary of a software developer : ₹ 50,000 per month
If E, D and C are the estimated development effort (in person-months), estimated development time (in months), and estimated development cost (in ₹ Lac) respectively, then (E, D, C) =_________.

Match the following in Software Engineering :
(a) Product Complexity
(b) Structured System Analysis
(c) Coupling and Cohesion
(d) Symbolic Execution
(i) Software Requirements Definition
(ii) Software Design
(iii) Validation Technique
(iv) Software Cost Estimation
explanation: Product complexity is a cost driver; structured analysis defines requirements; coupling/cohesion are design criteria; symbolic execution is a validation technique.

question: Which one of the following is not typically provided by Source Code Management Software ?
explanation: Syntax highlighting is an editor/IDE feature.

question: A software system crashed 20 times in the year 2017 and for each crash, it took 2 minutes to restart. Approximately, what was the software availability in that year ?
explanation: Downtime 40 minutes out of 525,600 minutes is 0.0076%, so availability ≈ 99.9924%.

question:
Match the 5 CMM Maturity levels/CMMI staged representations in List- I with their characterizations in List-II :
(a) Initial
(b) Repeatable
(c) Defined
(d) Managed
(e) Optimizing
(i) Processes are improved quantitatively and continually.
(ii) The plan for a project comes from a template for plans.
(iii) The plan uses processes that can be measured quantitatively.
(iv) There may not exist a plan or it may be abandoned.
(v) There's a plan and people stick to it.
explanation: Initial: no reliable plan; Repeatable: plan followed; Defined: plan from a standard template; Managed: quantitative measures; Optimizing: continual improvement.

question:
Coupling is a measure of the strength of the interconnections between software modules. Which of the following are correct statements with respect to module coupling ?
P: Common coupling occurs when one module controls the flow of another module by passing it information on what to do.
Q: In data coupling, the complete data structure is passed from one module to another through parameters.
R: Stamp coupling occurs when modules share a composite data structure and use only parts of it.

options.D: All of P, Q and R

explanation: P describes control coupling, so it is false. R is correct. Q is loosely worded (data coupling passes only the elementary data needed), but no option has R alone, so (3) Q and R is the intended answer.

question: A software design pattern often used to restrict access to an object is :
explanation: A protection proxy controls access to the real object.

question:
Reasons to re-engineer a software include :
P: Allow legacy software to quickly adapt to the changing requirements
Q: Upgrade to newer technologies/platforms/paradigm (for example, object-oriented)
R: Improve software maintainability
S: Allow change in the functionality and architecture of the software
explanation: Re-engineering improves structure and maintainability and moves software to new platforms without changing its functionality, so S is not a reason.

question: Which of the following is not a key strategy followed by the clean room approach to software development ?
explanation: Cleanroom uses static (formal) verification, not dynamic defect testing.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are True ?
P: Refactoring is the process of changing a software system in such a way that it does not alter the external behavior of the code yet improves the internal architecture.
Q: An example of refactoring is adding new features to satisfy a customer requirement discovered after a project is shipped.
explanation: Adding features changes behaviour, so it is not refactoring.

question:
The solution of the recurrence relation
T(m) = T(3m/4) + 1 is :
explanation: Master theorem case 2 with a = 1, b = 4/3: Θ(lg m).

question: Consider the array A=<4, 1, 3, 2, 16, 9, 10, 14, 8, 7>. After building heap from the array A, the depth of the heap and the right child of max-heap are _________ and _________ respectively. (Root is at level 0).
explanation: BUILD-MAX-HEAP gives 16, 14, 10, 8, 7, 9, 3, 2, 4, 1 (CLRS). With 10 nodes the depth is 3, and the root's right child is 10.

question: A hash function h defined h(key)=key mod 7, with linear probing, is used to insert the keys 44, 45, 79, 55, 91, 18, 63 into a table indexed from 0 to 6. What will be the location of key 18 ?
Which of the following algorithms solves the single-source shortest paths ?
explanation: Dijkstra solves single-source shortest paths; Floyd–Warshall and Johnson solve all pairs; Prim finds an MST.

question: A text is made up of the characters A, B, C, D, E each occurring with the probability 0.08, 0.40, 0.25, 0.15 and 0.12 respectively. The optimal coding technique will have the average length of :
A binary search tree in which every non-leaf node has non-empty left and right subtrees is called a strictly binary tree. Such a tree with 19 leaves :
explanation: A strictly binary tree with L leaves has 2L − 1 = 37 nodes.

question:
Match the following with respect to algorithm paradigms :
(a) The 8-Queen's problem
(b) Single-Source shortest paths
(c) STRASSEN's Matrix multiplication
(d) Optimal binary search trees
(i) Dynamic programming
(ii) Divide and conquer
(iii) Greedy approach
(iv) Backtracking
explanation: 8-queens: backtracking; SSSP (Dijkstra): greedy; Strassen: divide and conquer; OBST: dynamic programming.

question: The maximum number of comparisons needed to sort 9 items using radix sort is (assume each item is 5 digit octal number) :
A 5-ary tree is tree in which every internal node has exactly 5 children. The number of left nodes in such a tree with 8 internal nodes will be :
explanation: Leaves = (m − 1)i + 1 = 4 × 8 + 1 = 33. ('left nodes' is a misprint for 'leaf nodes'.)

question: Consider a Boolean function of ‘n’ variables. The order of an algorithm that determines whether the Boolean function produces a output 1 is :
explanation: In general all 2ⁿ input combinations may have to be tried (SAT), which is exponential.

question: Two finite state machines are said to be equivalent if they :

options.A: Have the same number of edges
options.B: Have the same number of states
options.C: Recognize the same set of tokens
options.D: Have the same number of states and edges

explanation: Equivalent automata accept the same language.

question:
The finite state machine given in figure below recognizes :
[4-state DFA: 'a' toggles between the left and right columns, 'b' toggles between the top and bottom rows; start state top-left, accepting state bottom-right]

options.A: any string of odd number of a's
options.B: any string of odd number of b's
options.C: any string of even number of a's and odd number of b's
options.D: any string of odd number of a's and odd number of b's

explanation: The accepting state is reached after an odd number of a's and an odd number of b's.

question: A pushdown automata behaves like a Turing machine when the number of auxiliary memory is :
explanation: A PDA with two (or more) stacks is equivalent to a Turing machine.

question: Pushdown automata can recognize language generated by_________.

options.C: Context free grammar or regular grammar

explanation: Regular languages are a subset of CFLs, so PDAs recognise both.

question: To obtain a string of n Terminals from a given Chomsky normal form grammar, the number of productions to be used is :
explanation: n − 1 binary productions plus n terminal productions = 2n − 1.

question:
Consider the following two Grammars :
G1 : S → SbS|a
G2 : S → aB|ab, A→GAB|a, B→ABb|b
Which of the following option is correct ?

options.C: Both G1 and G2 are ambiguous
options.D: Both G1 and G2 are not ambiguous

explanation: G1: 'ababa' has two parse trees. G2: 'ab' derives both as S → ab and as S → aB → ab.

question: Context sensitive language can be recognized by a :
explanation: CSLs correspond to linear bounded automata.

question: The set A={ 0ⁿ 1ⁿ 2ⁿ | n=1, 2, 3, ......... } is an example of a grammar that is :
explanation: 0ⁿ1ⁿ2ⁿ is the classic context-sensitive (not context-free) language.

question: A bottom-up parser generates :
explanation: LR (bottom-up) parsers trace a rightmost derivation in reverse.

question:
Consider the following statements( ) :
S1 : There exists no algorithm for deciding if any two Turing machines M1 and M2 accept the same language.
S2 : The problem of determining whether a Turing machine halts on any input is undecidable.
Which of the following options is correct ?

options.A: Both S1 and S2 are correct
options.B: Both S1 and S2 are not correct

explanation: TM equivalence and halting are both undecidable.

question: A slotted ALOHA network transmits 200-bit frames using a shared channel with a 200 Kbps bandwidth. Find the throughput of the system, if the system (all stations put together) produces 250 frames per second :
explanation: Frame time = 1 ms, so G = 0.25 and S = Ge^(−G) ≈ 0.195. The key takes 250 × 0.195 ≈ 49 frames/s. (Forouzan computes 1000 × 0.195 ≈ 195 frames/s, which is not offered.)

question: The period of a signal is 100 ms. Its frequency is _________.

The dotted-decimal notation of the following IPV4 address in binary notation is _________.
10000001 00001011 00001011 11101111

Which of the following statements are true ?
(a) Advanced Mobile Phone System (AMPS) is a second generation cellular phone system.
(b) IS - 95 is a second generation cellular phone system based on CDMA and DSSS.
(c) The Third generation cellular phone system will provide universal personnel communication.
explanation: AMPS is first generation (analog); (b) and (c) are true.

question:
Match the following symmetric block ciphers with corresponding block and key sizes :
(a) DES
(b) IDEA
(c) BLOW FISH
(d) AES
(i) block size 64 and key size ranges between 32 and 448
(ii) block size 64 and key size 64
(iii) block size 128 and key sizes 128, 192, 256
(iv) block size 64 and key size 128
explanation: DES: 64-bit block, 64-bit key (56 effective); IDEA: 64/128; Blowfish: 64-bit block, 32–448-bit key; AES: 128-bit block, 128/192/256-bit key.

question:
Which of the following statements are true ?
(a) Three broad categories of Networks are
(i) Circuit Switched Networks
(ii) Packet Switched Networks
(iii) Message Switched Networks
(b) Circuit Switched Network resources need not be reserved during the set up phase.
(c) In packet switching there is no resource allocation for packets.
explanation: Circuit switching reserves resources during setup, so (b) is false.

question: In Challenge-Response authentication the claimant ________.

options.A: Proves that she knows the secret without revealing it
options.B: Proves that she doesn't know the secret

explanation: The claimant answers the verifier's challenge with a response computed from the secret, without sending the secret itself.

question: Decrypt the message “WTAAD” using the Caesar Cipher with key=15.
explanation: Shifting each letter back 15 places: W→H, T→E, A→L, A→L, D→O = HELLO.

question: To guarantee correction of upto t errors, the minimum Hamming distance dmin in a block code must be ________.
explanation: Correcting t errors requires dmin = 2t + 1.

question:
Encrypt the Message “HELLO MY DEARZ” using Transposition Cipher with
Key: Plain Text 2 4 1 3 / Cipher Text 1 2 3 4
explanation: Blocks of 4 (ignoring spaces): HELL, OMYD, EARZ. Cipher positions 1–4 take plaintext positions 2, 4, 1, 3: ELHL, MDOY, AZER.

question: At a particular time of computation, the value of a counting semaphore is 10. Then 12 P operations and “x” V operations were performed on this semaphore. If the final value of semaphore is 7, x will be :

In a paged memory, the page hit ratio is 0.40. The time required to access a page in secondary memory is equal to 120 ns. The time required to access a page in primary memory is 15 ns. The average time required to access a page is ________.

In a multi-user operating system, 30 requests are made to use a particular resource per hour, on an average. The probability that no requests are made in 40 minutes, when arrival pattern is a poisson distribution, is _________.
explanation: λ = 30/hour, so in 40 minutes λt = 20, and P(0) = e⁻²⁰.

question: Normally user programs are prevented from handling I/O directly by I/O instructions in them. For CPUs having explicit I/O instructions, such I/O protection is ensured by having the I/O instructions privileged. In a CPU with memory mapped I/O, there is no explicit I/O instruction. Which one of the following is true for a CPU with memory mapped I/O ?

options.A: I/O protection is ensured by operating system routines.
options.B: I/O protection is ensured by a hardware trap.
options.C: I/O protection is ensured during system configuration.

explanation: The OS (via memory protection/mapping) keeps device addresses out of user programs' address space (GATE 2005).

question: Which UNIX/Linux command is used to make all files and sub-directories in the directory “progs” executable by all users ?
explanation: -R recurses and a+x adds execute permission for all users.

question:
Which of the following statements are true ?
(a) External Fragmentation exists when there is enough total memory space to satisfy a request but the available space is contiguous.
(b) Memory Fragmentation can be internal as well as external.
(c) One solution to external Fragmentation is compaction.
explanation: (a) should say 'not contiguous', so it is false.

question: Page information in memory is also called as Page Table. The essential contents in each entry of a page table is/are _________.

options.D: Both virtual page number and Page Frame Number

explanation: The PTE essentially holds the frame number; the virtual page number is the index, not a stored field.

question: Consider a virtual page reference string 1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 2, 5, 2, 3, 4. Suppose LRU page replacement algorithm is implemented with 3 page frames in main memory. Then the number of page faults are_________.
explanation: Faults occur on 1, 2, 3, 4 (evicting 1), 5 (evicting 3), 3 (evicting 4) and 4 (evicting 5): 7 in all.

question:
Consider the following three processes with the arrival time and CPU burst time given in milliseconds :
Process Arrival Time Burst Time
P1 0 7
P2 1 4
P3 2 8
The Gantt Chart for preemptive SJF scheduling algorithm is _________.
explanation: At t = 1 P2 (4) pre-empts P1 (6 remaining). P2 finishes at 5, then P1 (6) runs to 11, then P3 to 19.

question: In which of the following scheduling criteria, context switching will never take place ?
explanation: Non-pre-emptive SJF never forcibly switches a running process out (no pre-emptive context switch).

question: In RDBMS, which type of Join returns all rows that satisfy the join condition ?
explanation: An inner join returns exactly the rows satisfying the join condition.

question:
Consider a relation book (title, price) which contains the titles and prices of different books. Assuming that no two books have the same price, what does the following SQL query list ?
Select title
from book as B
where (select count (*)
 from book as T
 where T.price > B.price) < 7

options.A: Titles of the six most expensive books.
options.B: Title of the sixth most expensive books.
options.C: Titles of the seven most expensive books.
options.D: Title of the seventh most expensive books.

explanation: A book qualifies if fewer than 7 books cost more, i.e. it ranks 1st to 7th.

question: In a Hierachical database, a hashing function is used to locate the ________.
explanation: Key: (2). In hierarchical databases (e.g. IMS HDAM) a hashing (randomizing) routine locates the root segment of a record.

question: Relations produced from E - R Model will always be in ________.
explanation: Mapping guarantees only atomic values (1NF); higher normal forms depend on the design.

question:
Consider the following schedules involving two transactions.
S1 : r1(X) ; r1(Y) ; r2(X) ; r2(Y) ; w2(Y) ; w1(X)
S2 : r1(X) ; r2(X) ; r2(Y) ; w2(Y) ; r1(Y) ; w1(X)
Which one of the following statements is correct with respect to above ?

options.A: Both S1 and S2 are conflict serializable.
options.B: Both S1 and S2 are not conflict serializable.
options.C: S1 is conflict serializable and S2 is not conflict serializable.
options.D: S1 is not conflict serializable and S2 is conflict serializable.

explanation: S1: r1(Y)→w2(Y) gives T1→T2 and r2(X)→w1(X) gives T2→T1, a cycle. S2: all conflicts go T2→T1, so it is serializable.

question:
For a database relation R(a, b, c, d) where the domains of a, b, c and d include only atomic values, and only the following functional dependencies and those that can be inferred from them hold :
a→c
b→d
The relation is in _________.

options.A: First normal form but not in second normal form
options.B: Second normal form but not in third normal form

explanation: The key is ab and c, d depend on parts of it (partial dependencies).

question: A many-to-one relationship exists between entity sets r1 and r2. How will it be represented using functional depedencies if Pk(r) denotes the primary key attribute of relation r ?
explanation: Many r1 to one r2: each r1 entity determines its r2 entity.

question: Database systems that store each relation in a separate operating system file may use the operating system's authorization scheme, instead of defining a special scheme themselves. In this case, which of the following is false ?

options.A: The administrator enjoys more control on the grant option.
options.B: It is difficult to differentiate among the update, delete and insert authorizations.
options.C: Cannot store more than one relation in a file.
options.D: Operations on the database are speeded up as the authorization procedure is carried out at the operating system level.

explanation: With OS file permissions the DBA loses fine-grained control (e.g. over the grant option), so (1) is false (Korth exercise).

question:
Let R1(a, b, c) and R2(x, y, z) be two relations in which a is the foreign key of R1 that refers to the primary key of R2. Consider following four options.
(a) Insert into R1 (b) Insert into R2
(c) Delete from R1 (d) Delete from R2
Which of the following is correct about the referential integrity constraint with respect to above ?
explanation: Inserting a referencing tuple with no match, or deleting a referenced tuple, can violate referential integrity.

question: Consider a hash table of size seven, with starting index zero, and a hash function (7x+3) mod 4. Assuming the hash table is initially empty, which of the following is the contents of the table when the sequence 1, 3, 8, 10 is inserted into the table using closed hashing ? Here “__” denotes an empty location in the table.
In Artificial Intelligence (AI), an environment is uncertain if it is ________.

options.A: Not fully observable and not deterministic
options.B: Not fully observable or not deterministic

explanation: AIMA: an environment is uncertain if it is not fully observable or not deterministic.

question: In Artificial Intelligence (AI), a simple reflex agent selects actions on the basis of_________.

options.A: current percept, completely ignoring rest of the percept history.
options.B: rest of the percept history, completely ignoring current percept.
options.C: both current percept and complete percept history.
options.D: both current percept and just previous percept.

explanation: Simple reflex agents act on the current percept only.

question: In heuristic search algorithms in Artificial Intelligence (AI), if a collection of admissible heuristics h1.......hm is available for a problem and none of them dominates any of the others, which should we choose ?
explanation: The max of admissible heuristics is admissible and dominates each of them.

question:
Consider following sentences regarding A*, an informed search strategy in Artificial Intelligence (AI).
(a) A* expands all nodes with f(n) < C*.
(b) A* expands no nodes with f(n) ≥ C*.
(c) Pruning is integral to A*.
Here, C* is the cost of the optimal solution path.
Which of the following is correct with respect to the above statements ?

options.A: Both statement (a) and statement (b) are true.
options.B: Both statement (a) and statement (c) are true.
options.C: Both statement (b) and statement (c) are true.
options.D: All the statements (a), (b) and (c) are true.

explanation: AIMA: A* expands all nodes with f < C*, no nodes with f > C* (printed as ≥), and pruning is integral to it. The key accepts all three, though (b) is strictly about f > C*.

question:
Consider a vocabulary with only four propositions A, B, C and D. How many models are there for the following sentence ?
B∨C
explanation: 3 of the 4 (B, C) assignments satisfy B ∨ C, times 4 for A and D: 12.

question:
Consider the following statements :
(a) False ⊨ True
(b) If α ⊨ (β ∧ γ) then α ⊨ β and α ⊨ γ.
Which of the following is correct with respect to the above statements ?

options.A: Both statement (a) and statement (b) are false.
options.B: Statement (a) is true but statement (b) is false.
options.C: Statement (a) is false but statement (b) is true.
options.D: Both statement (a) and statement (b) are true.

explanation: False entails everything; entailing a conjunction entails each conjunct.

question:
Consider the following English sentence :
“Agra and Gwalior are both in India”.
A student has written a logical sentence for the above English sentence in First-Order Logic using predicate In(x, y), which means x is in y, as follows :
In(Agra, India) ∨ In(Gwalior, India)
Which one of the following is correct with respect to the above logical sentence ?

options.A: It is syntactically valid but does not express the meaning of the English sentence.
options.B: It is syntactically valid and expresses the meaning of the English sentence also.
options.C: It is syntactically invalid but expresses the meaning of the English sentence.
options.D: It is syntactically invalid and does not express the meaning of the English sentence.

explanation: The formula is well-formed, but ∨ should be ∧.

question:
Consider the following two sentences :
(a) The planning graph data structure can be used to give a better heuristic for a planning problem.
(b) Dropping negative effects from every action schema in a planning problem results in a relaxed problem.
Which of the following is correct with respect to the above sentences ?

options.A: Both sentence (a) and sentence (b) are false.
options.B: Both sentence (a) and sentence (b) are true.
options.C: Sentence (a) is true but sentence (b) is false.
options.D: Sentence (a) is false but sentence (b) is true.

explanation: Both are true (AIMA).

question:
A knowledge base contains just one sentence, ∃x AsHighAs (x, Everest). Consider the following two sentences obtained after applying existential instantiation.
(a) AsHighAs (Everest, Everest)
(b) AsHighAs (Kilimanjaro, Everest)
Which of the following is correct with respect to the above sentences ?

options.A: Both sentence (a) and sentence (b) are sound conclusions.
options.B: Both sentence (a) and sentence (b) are unsound conclusions.
options.C: Sentence (a) is sound but sentence (b) is unsound.
options.D: Sentence (a) is unsound but sentence (b) is sound.

explanation: Existential instantiation must use a new Skolem constant; substituting existing constants is unsound in both cases (AIMA exercise).

question: Consider the set of all possible five-card poker hands dealt fairly from a standard deck of fifty-two cards. How many atomic events are there in the joint probability distribution ?
E is the number of edges in the graph and f is maximum flow in the graph. When the capacities are integers, the runtime of Ford-Fulberson algorithm is bounded by :
explanation: Each augmentation costs O(E) and increases the flow by at least 1, giving O(E·f).

question: Which of the following statements is false about convex minimization problem ?

options.A: If a local minimum exists, then it is a global minimum
options.B: The set of all global minima is convex set
options.C: The set of all global minima is concave set
options.D: For each strictly convex function, if the function has a minimum, then the minimum is unique

explanation: The set of minima of a convex function is convex, not 'concave'.

question:
The following LPP
Maximize z=100x1+2x2+5x3
Subject to
14x1+x2−6x3+3x4=7
32x1+x2−12x3≤10
3x1−x2−x3≤0
x1, x2, x3, x4≥0
has
explanation: With x1 = x2 = 0 and x4 = (7 + 6x3)/3, every constraint holds for any x3 ≥ 0, so z = 5x3 grows without bound.

question: Digital data received from a sensor can fill up 0 to 32 buffers. Let the sample space be S={0, 1, 2, .........., 32} where the sample j denote that j of the buffers are full and p(i) = (33−i)/561. Let A denote the event that the even number of buffers are full. Then p(A) is :

The equivalence of
¬ ∃ x Q (x) is :
explanation: De Morgan for quantifiers: ¬∃x Q(x) ≡ ∀x ¬Q(x).

question:
If Ai={−i, ... −2,−1, 0, 1, 2, . . . . . i}
then ∪(i=1 to ∞) Ai is :
explanation: The union contains every integer: Z.

question:
Match the following in List - I and List - II, for a function f :
(a) ∀x ∀y (f (x)=f (y) → x=y)
(b) ∀y ∃x (f (x)=y)
(c) ∀x f (x)=k
(i) Constant
(ii) Injective
(iii) Surjective
explanation: (a) is one-to-one, (b) is onto, (c) is constant.

question: Which of the relations on {0, 1, 2, 3} is an equivalence relation ?
explanation: The identity relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; the others fail reflexivity or transitivity.

question: Which of the following is an equivalence relation on the set of all functions from Z to Z ?

options.D: { (f, g) | f (x)−g (x)=k for some k ∈ Z }
